title: CRLR/101/2013 of Kulwant Singh Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
CRLR No. 101 of 2013
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Jitendra Chaudhary, Advocate for
the petitioner.
Mr. Pratiroop Pandey, A.G.A for the
State of Uttarakhand.
The revisionist in the present criminal
revision has challenged the order dated
04.05.2013 passed by the Additional District &
Sessions Judge, Haridwar, whereby, while
allowing the revision of respondent no. 2 has
set aside the order dated 20.12.2012 as passed
by the Judicial Magistrate, Haridwar, in
Complaint Case No. 77/11 'Jeet Singh vs.
Srawan Singh & Others' under Sections 420,
467 and 468 of IPC registered at P.S. Syampur,
District Haridwar, whereby, the revisional court
has remanded the matter back to the Trial Court
to reconsider and pass a fresh order.
As against the order passed by the
Judicial Magistrate on 20.12.2012 when the
revision was preferred by the respondent on
03.12.2012, it was admitted and notices were
issued for summoning the records of the Court
below as well as notice were issued to all the
opposite private respondents.
On perusal of the entire order sheet the
order dated 26.04.2013 shows that the
revisionist has not even taken steps to serve
opposite parties no. 3 to 6 of the revision, in
which the petitioner was placed as opposite
party no. 4 and due to non taking of steps to
serve respondent nos. 3 to 6, it would be
deemed from the records that the present
revisionist was not heard at the time when the
impugned order of remand dated 04.05.2013
was passed.

On this limited ground itself, when the
revisionist was not giving prior notice by the
revisional court while passing the order dated
04.05.2013 and setting aside the order of the
Judicial Magistrate dated 20.10.2012, the order
dated 04.05.2013 is set aside.
The matter is remitted back to the
revisional court and the revisional court would
direct the revisionist to take fresh steps for
serving the opposite party and only after
ensuring an effective service all the respondents
to the revision, the revision would be decided
on merits.
Subject to the above observations, the
revision succeeds and is allowed and the
impugned order of remand dated 04.05.2013 is
quashed.
However, there would be no order as to
cost.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 10.05.2019
Pooja
